svg.title: How a pick is made, in six steps. 1. The cart changes, and after a 500 ms debounce the front end posts the cart names to POST /recommendations/. 2. Rule match: each cart item is matched against RECOMMENDATION_RULES, 13 cart keys each with 3 pairings, and products are found with a SQL LIKE query, skipping anything already in the cart. 3. The top 5 candidates are kept. 4. Cache: an MD5 key of the sorted cart and candidate ids, kept for 5 minutes, so the same cart never pays for the same LLM call twice. 5. The LLM, DeepSeek V3 through OpenRouter, ranks and enriches the candidates with confidence, why, when, best for, review summary, pros and cons, using customer reviews. 6. The top 3 come back as AI Picks. Cart keys: Milk, Bread, Eggs, Yogurt, Tomatoes, Bananas, Coffee, Chocolate, Rice, Chips, Cheese, Butter, Berries. Example pairings: Bread to Almond Butter, Rice to Schezwan Sauce, Chips to Sparkling Water Lime.

section.h2: Rules pick the shelf. The model explains the choice.
section.p: Every cart change runs the same short pipeline. Teal steps are deterministic, berry steps involve the language model.

div.p: Then POST /recommendations/ with the cart names.
Each cart item maps to 3 pairings, found by SQL LIKE. Items already in the cart are skipped.
De duplicated, in rule priority order.
Same cart, same candidates: no second LLM call.
Reads the reviews, returns confidence, why, when, best for, pros and cons as JSON.
Shown in the cart drawer with the reasoning attached.

div.div: Hand written pairings. They work with no key at all.
Bread → Almond Butter · Rice → Schezwan Sauce · Chips → Sparkling Water Lime · Coffee → Dark Chocolate Bar 70%
